description: The line plot illustrates the performance of three models—20NG, IMDB, and NIPS—measured by the NPMI (Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information) metric as a function of the “weight of negative sampling,” which ranges from 0.5 to 3.0 on the linear x-axis. The y-axis, labeled “NPMI,” spans from 0.18 to 0.42, with a break indicated between 0.22 and 0.38, suggesting a non-continuous scale to emphasize variation in the higher range. The 20NG model (black squares connected by solid lines) starts at approximately NPMI = 0.37 at weight 0.5, rises slightly to 0.38 at weight 1.5, dips to 0.37 at weight 2.0, and ends at 0.38 at weight 3.0. The IMDB model (red circles connected by solid lines) begins at NPMI ≈ 0.195 at weight 0.5, drops to 0.19 at weight 1.0, peaks at 0.20 at weight 1.5, dips again to 0.195 at weight 2.0, and stabilizes at 0.195 at weight 3.0. The NIPS model (blue triangles connected by solid lines) starts at NPMI ≈ 0.40 at weight 0.5, rises to 0.41 at weight 1.0, remains flat at 0.41 through weight 1.5, declines slightly to 0.405 at weight 2.0, and ends at 0.405 at weight 3.0. Overall, NIPS consistently achieves the highest NPMI scores across all weights, followed by 20NG, while IMDB remains the lowest.
